context: This seven-day sample is separate from the earlier November 18–19 experiment. Both November 4 runs start with empty stores and process the same 287 submitted works. The second run uses revised guidance. Enrichment, grouping checks and summaries all ran again, so membership changes cannot be attributed to a single wording change.

review.finding: The short description characterizes NGC 5408 X-2 as an obscured ultraluminous X-ray source. The paper proposes that interpretation for a candidate.

The short description assigns abundance, stellar ages, ionized gas and sizes to each paper. Three linked OASIS papers report different observables from a common observing program. Feedback is an interpretation argued particularly in Paper II.

Headline and short account retain the measured quiet phases at z>4. The short account separates observations from a forecast near z=14. The long account separately attributes the counts and stellar ages, ionized gas and feedback interpretation, and sizes. The independent model counts as theoretical support, not another observation.

All three are observing proposals and the short account keeps that status. One targets abundances of quiescent galaxies, another the sites of transients, another globular clusters in ultra-diffuse galaxies. A common proposed instrument is too broad a basis for calling these one physical question.

The three studies use measured data to examine connections between active galactic nuclei and host-galaxy properties. The detailed account attributes correlations, inferred structure and alternative interpretations to the respective samples.

The excluded candidate combined stellar chemical abundances, skew spectra, the global 21-cm signal, misspecified cosmic-dawn inference and radio recombination lines. No three addressed a single observable and physical question.

decision: Keep the stellar/galactic scope in the Physics pilot. The new source and the revised synthesis pass selected checks while grouping by proposed facility remains an observed failure. This is an editorial spot check, not the ten high / ten low / ten excluded acceptance review.
